data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's definitive test — 'removing the claim from the checker's input would change the checker's output; if not, it is restatement' — is incoherent under the covering principle that verification must produce an output not derivable from the claim's surface form. Any genuine execution or count produces a world-dependent result (e.g., a raw count, a program exit code) that is independent of the claim text, so removing the claim from the input cannot change that result; the test would classify every real execution as 'restatement.' Conversely, a paraphrase whose wording shifts because the claim is absent would pass SRC_001's test, yet is paradigmatic restatement. The counter-screen (requiring execution/count evidence elsewhere) partially patches this, but SRC_001 still elevates the broken counterfactual as 'the definitive test,' directly contradicting its own principle.
